title: Functions & arrows
description: Three ways to declare callable code: function declarations, expressions, and arrows — plus how each handles this, default params, and implicit returns.

notes: Arrows do NOT bind their own this — they capture this from the enclosing scope.
Implicit return only works with a single expression body (no braces).
Function declarations are hoisted; expressions and arrows assigned to const are NOT — calling them before assignment throws ReferenceError.

options: Binds it to the global object
